LoFreq 2.1.5 (LoFreq_Star): lofreq
Licence: MIT (LICENSE in this folder). Built with HTSlib 1.24 (LICENSE.htslib; with htscodecs, LICENSE.htscodecs),
zlib 1.3.1 (LICENSE.zlib) and two long-double functions of OpenLibm 0.8.8 (LICENSE.openlibm); LoFreq contains uthash
(LICENSE.uthash) and DCDFLIB (NOTICE.cdflib). The loader is Emscripten's runtime (MIT and NCSA: LICENSE.emscripten).
THIRD_PARTY_LICENSES.txt lists them.
Upstream source: https://github.com/CSB5/lofreq (tag v2.1.5, commit 8fe42b04dcd9775fb618d8004649421c0632b35c)

Compiled to WebAssembly by the genomics-wasm project (https://github.com/comparativechrono/genomics-wasm,
commit bfacba3): Emscripten 3.1.64, one thread. The module (lofreq.mjs, lofreq.wasm) is used here as that project
built it: the page runs each command in a worker of its own (assets/js/threads-worker.mjs). Everything needed to
build it again is described in ../../../licenses/genomics-wasm-build/.

Changes to the source (tools/lofreq/browser.patch there): lofreq call runs LoFreq's filter as a function, where
upstream starts "lofreq filter" through a shell (the same thresholds and options); the C library's floating-point
exception flags, which WebAssembly does not have, are recorded explicitly where LoFreq checks them; the test counts
of filter and uniq are 64-bit numbers. WebAssembly's long double expl and log10l would lose very small
probabilities, so OpenLibm's functions are linked in their place. Calling and filtering are unchanged.
"lofreq somatic", "call-parallel" and "vcfplot" are Python scripts upstream. lofreq-somatic.mjs (MIT, from
genomics-wasm's runtime/, unchanged) is the translation of lofreq2_somatic.py that runs the somatic workflow's
commands – call, filter, vcfset, uniq – one after another; index.mjs is the workbench's small part of it (the paths
of the terminal: see the comment in it). call-parallel and vcfplot are not available.

In the workbench's terminal, lofreq somatic --threads N is run with one thread, with a note, and the messages of its
steps stay out of sight unless it fails (as upstream, whose log files keep them).

Checked against LoFreq 2.1.5 built natively from the same sources (genomics-wasm's comparison: 20 of 20 cases with
the HCC1395 tumour/normal reads, among them complete somatic workflows run by upstream's own Python script; and in the
workbench with the example data): lofreq call gives the same VCF records, lofreq indelqual the same BAM file byte for
byte, and lofreq somatic the same files with the same records.
